evidence.quote: F. NOx RACT Requirements Danisco operates three mid -size boilers (Boilers #3, #4, and #5) that are licensed to fire distillate fuel and natural gas. Boiler #3 (also known as Unit #20 or E9030) was manufactured by Union Iron Works in 1966 with a heat input capacity of 85.6 MMBtu/hr. Boiler #4 (also known as Unit #21 or E9040) was manufactured by Union Iron Works in 1965 with a heat input capacity of 48.6 MMBtu/hr. Boiler #5 (also known as Unit #22 or E9050) was manufactured by Union Iron Works in 1963 with a heat input capacity of 48.4 MMBtu/hr. The boilers were all originally designed to fire #6 fuel oil. However, New Source Review License A-366-77-6-A (issued 3/26/14) addressed the conversion of the boilers from firing #6 fuel oil to firing natural gas or distillate fuel. With this conversion, the ability to fire #6 fuel oil was removed from the facility. Revisions to 06-096 C.M.R. ch. 138 went into effect May 7, 2025. These changes included the establishment of new standards for emission units located within the 2022 Ozone Transport Region, as defined in that chapter. Danisco is located within the 2022 Ozone Transport Region. Danisco must either comply with the new applicable standards in 06-096 C.M.R. ch. 138, § 4 by May 1, 2026, or apply for and receive approval of an alternative RACT determination pursuant to 06-096 C.M.R. ch. 138, § 4(H). Danisco has elected to comply with the applicable requirements in section 4 of the rule. Boilers #3 is a mid-size boiler with a heat input less than 100 MMBtu/hr and fires only distillate fuel and natural gas . Boilers #4 and #5 are small boilers each with a heat input less than 50 MMBtu/hr. Pursuant to 06- 096 C.M.R. ch. 138, §§ 4(B)(1) and 4(C), these boilers are each subject to the following work practice standards in section 4(C) of the rule. 1. Each boiler shall be equipped with an oxygen trim system that automatically maintains an optimum air-to-fuel ratio. 2. Danisco shall perform a boiler tune -up at least once every five years. The first boiler tune-up is due no later than May 1, 2031. A tune -up conducted to comply with 40 C.F.R. Part 63, Subpart JJJJJJ shall satisfy this requirement provided it complies with the requirements of the following paragraph.

question: Draft a buyer finding for facility-017 after the Danisco transfer: how do retained renewal reporting, conditional certification and new salt duties constrain a claim of inherited-obligation clearance?
answer: The transfer is subject to attached conditions. Renewal semiannual reports are dueJan31/Jul31 with a deviations/correction summary; timely means postmarked by due date or received within seven calendar days. Annual certification dueJan31 has the same timing rule, using required tests/monitoring; other reasonably available information is allowed only when the stated data/request conditions are met. Later salt controls and concurrent term remain scoped, not measured compliance. Request submitted reports, underlying logs/test/request evidence, current orders and actual operation before any inherited-obligation or all-program clearance conclusion.

question: Separate facility-017’s bulk-salt60day information duty,18month construction clock and later Part70 incorporation. Do March2026 application receipts establish the construction-clock start or an actual deadline breach?
answer: NSR10’s July1,2026 order has a conditional additional-information duty within60days of a Department written request unless the letter states otherwise. Construction approval becomes invalid if not commenced within18months after receipt of approval or discontinued18months, subject to possible extension. March24/30 are application receipt/acceptance, not stated approval-receipt or construction dates. September1,2026 Part70 incorporation has a concurrent KR term. Obtain request letters, approval delivery, actual construction/discontinuance and extensions; no unconditional60day filing, computed breach or completed project follows from signatures/application dates alone.
